name: product-feature-registry
purpose: Defines the installable desktop product as a Git-backed AI workspace tracker whose primary value is importing many repositories, launching replaceable AI coding tools, and showing current work, evidence, validation, reports, and terminal state. Agent and tool operations are separated into agent-platform.

reader_guide.summary: Use this registry before changing the desktop home screen, snapshot schema, installer shell runtime, or platform feature navigation.
how_to_read: Read product_position first to understand what the product is and what it is not.
Read feature_layers to see which capabilities are primary product features and which capabilities are supporting surfaces.
Read promotion_loop before adding workflow, prompt, tool, skill, or agent creation features.
Read structure_rules before naming a feature, tab, data store, or installer shell behavior as monitoring.
Use validation_gates as the acceptance checklist when making a UI, data, or runtime change around these features.
update_triggers: The desktop home screen or first-run product promise changes.
A feature is promoted from workflow, prompt, template, tool, skill, or agent into a desktop product surface.
A new workspace import, CLI adapter, Git status, work report, evidence, learning, or observability capability is added.
Agent factory, tool studio, direct provider execution, or Ollama management starts to look like the main desktop product again.
The installer shell runtime contract changes how work state, decisions, evidence, validation, or evaluations are accumulated.

structure_rules.rule: The desktop product shall be positioned as a Git workspace tracker for guest AI coding tools and current work reports, not as an all-in-one agent factory, tool runtime, model manager, or monitoring dashboard.
structure_rules.reason: The user explicitly said the main purpose is helping people use many AI coding tools over Git workspaces and inspect current work outputs.

structure_rules.rule: The first product surface shall foreground Git workspace import/open/clone/create, terminal and guest AI tool launch, work timeline, reports, evidence, and requirements.
structure_rules.reason: The user asked for a simple interface that starts work instead of making them configure platform internals first.

structure_rules.rule: Existing shell, source review, runtime data, decision inbox, history, requirements, and monitoring pieces shall be surfaced as named product features with a clear primary, root-tool, visibility, or supporting role.
structure_rules.reason: The product should stop scattering surfaces as implementation leftovers and should expose them as sellable feature modules.

structure_rules.rule: Current work visibility, history, reports, documents, requirements, and diagnostics shall support the workspace tracker's main promise: understanding what is happening now and why.
structure_rules.reason: The user said current work summaries, plans, reports, and evidence are central to the desktop app after the product split.

structure_rules.rule: Operator, monitoring, document, requirement, project registry, and structure surfaces shall live behind a dedicated Operator Center or settings-style surface instead of the primary work navigation.
structure_rules.reason: A sellable desktop app should foreground agent work and keep admin/review surfaces available without making them feel like the product.

structure_rules.rule: Agent creation, capability promotion, evaluation, work history, and improvement records shall be designed as a continuous product loop, not as static documentation.
structure_rules.reason: The product must make agents easier to create and continuously improve through accumulated data.

structure_rules.rule: Configuration and setup should be handled through dedicated settings, capability, or modal surfaces instead of being spread across one dashboard screen.
structure_rules.reason: A desktop app should separate work execution, configuration, and review surfaces like mature desktop tools do.

structure_rules.rule: Agent factory, root tool management, provider direct agent execution, Ollama model management, and AWS AgentCore-style runtime lifecycle shall be treated as separated advanced platform capabilities.
structure_rules.reason: The user asked to remove these from the default desktop app and build them as a separate platform.

structure_rules.rule: Already defined agents shall be exposed as runnable desktop product surfaces before asking the user to create another agent.
structure_rules.reason: The user asked to easily run the existing search agent instead of hunting through configs or shell commands.

Observable signals proving the platform is improving instead of only showing status.

product_position.primary_claim: A desktop workspace tracker for importing or creating Git-backed projects, launching Codex, Claude Code, Cursor, Antigravity, Gemini CLI, OpenCode, and other replaceable guest AI coding tools, then showing current work, task order, evidence, validation, reports, terminal state, and Git boundaries in one simple app.

desktop_home_surface.home_copy_rule: The first screen shall emphasize Git workspace import, current work timeline, CLI/terminal launch, evidence, validation, reports, and Git project boundaries. Agent factory and Tool Studio shall be advanced/operator surfaces.
desktop_home_surface.configuration_rule: Execution settings shall focus on workspace path, Git repository state, and guest AI tool adapters. Provider direct execution, Ollama, agent factory, and tool builder controls are separated from the default user path.

feature_layers.label: Guest AI Tool Orchestration
feature_layers.purpose: Launch and track replaceable guest AI coding surfaces such as Codex, Claude Code, Gemini CLI, Cursor, Antigravity, and OpenCode over the selected Git workspace with bounded IO, decision routing, merge gates, and cleanup.
feature_layers.user_outcome: The user chooses the workspace and preferred AI tool, starts the work from one place, and sees terminal state, decisions, evidence, and reports without being locked to one assistant.
automation_targets: terminal and external editor launch from the selected Git workspace
provider credential references only when a guest adapter needs them
top-level run configuration selection for search agent, CLI session, task pipe, and workspace readiness
Services-style inspection of runtime, workspace, adapters, providers, and active sessions
Problems-style surfacing of missing runtime, missing adapters, missing model accounts, pending decisions, dirty drafts, and release blockers
AgentCore-style blueprint to native agent proposal creation
local Python agent execution with remote services treated as tool connectors
production agent blueprint selection for runtime, memory, gateway, and evaluation patterns
validation_gates: search agent work-chat exposes research-insight-planner-agent
Desktop Runtime exposes IntelliJ-style Run Configuration, Services, Problems, and status bar controls before long scrolling panels
local/provider models can produce task-run records without requiring a shell command
readiness test includes product feature architecture
resource guard covers long-running lanes
customer snapshot preserves feature claims without internal source
Agents screen exposes AgentCore-style production blueprint controls
Applying a production blueprint fills Search Agent Work Chat and Agent Core inputs
Creating an AgentCore-style proposal uses the native Agent Core proposal writer

feature_layers.label: Agent Work Environment
feature_layers.purpose: Host imported and newly created Git repositories, runtime data stores, task-run records, decisions, support diagnostics, and workspace-scoped reports.
feature_layers.user_outcome: The user can open many Git-backed workspaces, see which repository is active, and keep summaries, plans, reports, terminal sessions, and evidence attached to the right project.
validation_gates: workspace boundary commands reject unsafe paths
resident desktop/source panels share native workspace warmup and prepare requests
storage architecture keeps durable repository knowledge file-backed while moving operational indexes toward embedded SQLite
accumulated data manifest is persisted
customer bundle excludes platform source

feature_layers.label: Agent Development Environment
feature_layers.purpose: Provide the developer workbench for source review, multi-file edits, diffs, templates, requirements, specs, validation, and runtime contracts.
feature_layers.user_outcome: The user can shape agent platform behavior inside a desktop workbench instead of bouncing between loose files and terminal-only flows.
validation_gates: Monaco code workbench is not only an embed
file writes stay within workspace root
requirements and specs trace product feature changes

feature_layers.label: Agent Core
feature_layers.purpose: Turn repeated work into prompts, workflows, templates, tools, skills, agents, and platform features inside the separate agent-platform product.
feature_layers.user_outcome: Advanced users can still create agents and reusable capabilities, but this no longer dominates the default desktop tracker experience.
learning_signals: agent proposal saved from AgentCore-style blueprint
validation_gates: candidate has source evidence and rollback plan
skill or agent validation passes
promotion selects the smallest useful asset first
Agent Core can be prefilled from a selected production blueprint
AgentCore Quick Builder can call the native agent proposal writer from the selected blueprint

feature_layers.label: Learning & Evaluation Loop
feature_layers.purpose: Accumulate work history, timing, evaluations, web searches, summaries, request traces, evidence, and reports so every workspace shows what happened and why.
feature_layers.user_outcome: The user can see the current work summary, ordered plan, evidence, validation result, report trail, and remaining gaps without reading raw folders first.
validation_gates: intent maps show source freshness
evaluations cite validation outcomes
new product work creates request trace and work summary
fundamental improvement structure sanitizes customer snapshots
AI Eval tab shows current score, history comparison, token/tool comparison, and open-source EVAL candidates

feature_layers.label: Root Tool Management
feature_layers.purpose: Keep tool building, Python venvs, deployment, provider direct execution, and advanced tool registry work in the separate agent-platform product while the desktop tracker keeps only simple guest-adapter setup.
feature_layers.user_outcome: The default desktop app stays focused on workspaces and reports; advanced tool operations remain available in their own platform.
automation_targets: root tool sharing across task-specific agents
validation_gates: Home and execution settings expose root tools separately from the workspace tracker default flow
root tools stay reusable across task-specific agents and guest CLI lanes
Tool Studio renders source-backed agent tool usage playbooks

feature_layers.label: Provider Direct Agent Run
feature_layers.purpose: Keep direct provider API execution, model-task runs, and provider account experiments in the separated agent platform instead of the default workspace tracker path.
feature_layers.user_outcome: The default user can launch guest coding tools without being forced to configure raw provider execution first.
validation_gates: provider direct run is not part of default user navigation
provider account state remains available as advanced setup

feature_layers.label: Ollama Model Management
feature_layers.purpose: Keep local model runtime selection, Ollama endpoint management, and model install decisions in the separated agent/tool platform.
feature_layers.user_outcome: The default desktop tracker does not block first use on local model setup while advanced users can still connect local model runtimes.
validation_gates: Ollama remains optional and advanced
workspace tracker works without local model installation

feature_layers.label: AgentCore Runtime Lifecycle
feature_layers.purpose: Keep AWS AgentCore-style runtime, gateway, identity, memory, tool, browser/code tool, evaluation, and policy lifecycle as separated platform infrastructure.
feature_layers.user_outcome: The desktop app can reference production agent blueprints without becoming an AWS runtime console.
validation_gates: AgentCore-style lifecycle is separated from default user navigation
AWS deployment remains optional and explicit

feature_layers.label: Work Visibility
feature_layers.purpose: Show active work, current repository, deferred decisions, task-run records, report status, evidence status, and terminal state at a glance so work is not forgotten.
feature_layers.user_outcome: The user can immediately see what is running, what is blocked, what was planned, what was validated, and where to resume.
validation_gates: Home shows current workload before operator documents
CLI orchestration surface keeps task-run and decision counts visible
Desktop Runtime run records and decisions are grouped into a timeline before raw logs

feature_layers.label: Observability & Monitoring
feature_layers.purpose: Expose structure, history, documents, source inventory, diagnostics, and status so the primary agent platform features can be understood and trusted.
feature_layers.user_outcome: The user can inspect accumulated data and platform state without mistaking that inspection layer for the whole product.
validation_gates: observability role remains supporting
customer snapshot removes internal source
readiness scripts check supporting role
parallel snapshot collection keeps deterministic output and synchronous fallback

promotion_loop.improvement_rule: When repeated human work, agent failures, omitted steps, validation failures, or useful patterns recur, create the smallest durable asset first and promote only when evidence justifies a larger feature.

quality_signals: The first screen names Git workspaces, guest AI tool launch, current work timeline, reports, evidence, and requirements before agent/tool runtime internals.
Tool Studio gives root tools, Python runtime setup, provider direct run, Ollama, and deployment their own separated platform surface.
Current work volume, deferred decisions, task-run records, and agent count are visible at a glance.
Snapshot data includes product feature architecture for developer and customer builds.
Customer snapshot preserves sellable feature structure but removes internal source paths and validation internals.
Readiness tests fail if the desktop product drifts away from workspace_tracker or if separated platform functions return to default user navigation.
New feature work updates requirements, specs, validation, history, and request traces.
AgentCore-style blueprint choices map reference samples to runnable local product flows.
Desktop Runtime starts from run configurations and tool-window status instead of making the user scan a web dashboard.
Resident desktop/source panels share native warmup and source-catalog prepare requests instead of duplicating OS work.
AWS deployment remains optional; the installed desktop app owns task state and accumulated records.

validation_gates.validates: Product feature registry keeps workspace_tracker as the primary product and separated agent/tool/runtime capabilities out of the default user path.
Workspace snapshot collector exposes product feature architecture and customer snapshot sanitization.
Customer bundle keeps product feature structure while stripping internal documents, source files, and implementation-only paths.

validation_gates.validates: Agents UI and product registries expose AgentCore-style production blueprints and quick proposal creation without making AWS mandatory.
Desktop Runtime keeps the IntelliJ-style run configuration, Services, Problems, and status bar surface wired into real actions.
